los.text: Explain the principles of breaking bad news, demonstrating an understanding of effective communication strategies, patient empathy, and the importance of maintaining emotional support during difficult conversations.
los.html:
SPIKESDetail
SettingPrivate room, sit down, no interruptions (bleep to a colleague), tissues, invite a relative/friend, nurse present
Perception"What do you understand about why we did the scan?"
Invitation"Would you like me to go through the results?" (how much they want to know)
Knowledge
  • Warning shot ("I'm afraid it's not the news we were hoping for")
  • Then give the news in plain language
  • Small chunks
  • Pause and allow silence
EmotionsRecognise and respond with empathy ("I can see this is a huge shock"); allow time
Strategy and summaryNext steps, support, written information, key worker/CNS contact, follow-up; check understanding
  • Avoid: jargon, euphemisms, false reassurance, rushing. Document what was said and who was present.

los.text: Apply clinical knowledge and problem-solving skills to solve a range of medical clues in a simulated escape room scenario, demonstrating teamwork, critical thinking, and effective decision-making under time pressure
los.html:
• Escape-room style cases test problem solving under pressure: read the clues carefully
    • prioritise (ABCDE thinking)
    • divide tasks within the team
    • communicate clearly (closed-loop)
    • reason through differentials
    • and review mistakes afterwards.

los.text: Perform a clinical examination of the cranial nerves with increased confidence and accuracy.
los.html:
• Cranial nerve examination: see ICM Year 1 › Neurology & cognition › LO 8. "Increased confidence": a fluent order (I–XII), each test explained to the patient, and interpretation: e.g. LMN facial weakness with forehead involvement = Bell's palsy
    • tongue deviation towards the lesion = XII palsy
    • bitemporal hemianopia = chiasmal lesion.
